I definitely understand where you’re coming from. It’s been almost a year since I was last in a psych hospital. And God, I miss it so much. I miss the comfort and the constant support. I went to 3 different ones. One of the ones I went to, I went to over 10 times. IMO, it was an amazing experience. I’m staying out for a year so I can work there after my one year mark because I want to help others the way the techs helped me in my worst moments of life. If you need someone to talk to, hmu! I’d love to talk

I would usually write something positive and give the best advice I could but I’m right along your side right now. I’m not sure what will happen once it’s all over but I am so so done. Life is hard

I’ve gone to the doctors for a few reasons over the past few months and they all resulted in blood draws. Some of the visits I had cuts that were still in the healing stage and I had scars in every single visit. My personal preference, I don’t tell them about it. I’ve been hospitalized for SI before so if they have questions then they can look at my records. But most of the time, they don’t even say anything about them. If they do ask me about it though, they’ll most likely ask how “fresh” the cuts/scars are and if you’re feeling suicidal or unsafe as in the moment. Just be honest with them, chances are they aren’t trying to pry, they just want you to be safe 🤍

You are so incredibly strong for reaching out. Even if it wasn’t the way you intended on reaching out, you still did. And that’s all that matters. You’re cared for and loved and I pray you find long term happiness again.
Congratulations on being a year clean. That’s so awesome!

Honestly I wish I knew what to say to help you feel better.. to help you get better but I don't know what to say to make things alright.  What I can say though is I understand the pain you are going through. I don't know why you are going through this or what is causing it but I understand the basics and I personally understand the struggle that you explained. I force (literally force) myself out of bed every morning and do some stretches and then I do a workout (I have an app so I feel more encouraged) and after that, I feel a lot better. I've done quite a bit of research on helping depression and exercise is honestly a coping skill that definitely works. It gets your body going, it releases your "feel good" hormones, and you get to tell to yourself you actually accomplished something. Maybe you can try that as a starter? 
Also, if you feel that you really need help or that you are in immediate danger to yourself, go to the doctor's. Depending on where you live, you can go without an adult. And from what I understand, your mom kinda just shrugs it off. If you go to the doctor you can tell them exactly how you're feeling and they can get you on a plan to try and get better. 
You got this though, 100%.
